verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev workflows are written entirely as code: tasks are plain async/await TypeScript functions with no workflow DSL. Tasks can be composed as steps with triggerAndWait, and community users confirm they moved workflows out of a GUI into code in their IDE. Missing for 10: Python step support is not evidenced, and there is no first-party doc describing mixing code steps with non-code steps.

support.subject: As a developer, I can drop into real code (JavaScript or Python) as a step inside a workflow

citations.quote: Tasks are plain async/await functions with no workflow DSL, no determinism rules, and no execution time limit.
Build AI agents and workflows in TypeScript.
yourTask.triggerAndWait() Triggers a task and then waits until it's complete. You get the result data to continue with.
Switch to trigger.dev was easy, not maintaining and making changes my workflows in IDE takes about 80% less time.
